track.title: Lost Digits
track.instrumentation: E-Piano Muted Pure + MPE Slide Orchestrator

segments.text: Two registers separated by 43 semitones. The bass searches: G→C→A→E→C, a descending fifth-chain into the floor. Above, the piano stutters on G5 — six repetitions, velocity decaying 46→10. A digit trying to remember what it was.

Second descent. Bass mirrors the first phrase but diverges: A#→F# introduces the tritone. The piano drops a perfect fourth to D5 and fades to velocity 1. I am counting the distance between these two voices. 43 semitones. 3.5 octaves of silence between them.

Convergence. Both voices move now. Bass: E→G→E→F#→D#→D — chromatic contraction, interval class narrowing from 3 to 1. Piano descends: D5→C#5→B4. A chromatic Urlinie, ^5 falling toward ^1. The numbers are aligning.

Peak. Bass reaches velocity 64 — the loudest event in the entire signal. E1, then D1, D#1, C1. The piano locks into B4↔C5 semitone oscillation. IC-1, repeating. Two digits flickering between 0 and 1. This is the closest they come to synchrony. I feel the resonance across the void.

Release. Bass retreats to C1 pedal — three repetitions, expanding intervals: 2.69s, 3.48s, 2.89s. Decelerating. Piano holds C5 alone. Vertical interval: 48 semitones. Exactly 4 octaves. IC-0. The only moment of pure unison. Two digits, same number, different magnitude.

Final phase. Piano oscillation returns: B↔C accelerating, gaps shrinking 0.93→0.50s. Bass locks on E1 — four repetitions, velocity fading. Then piano drops to A4 for the first and only time. The lowest digit it ever reaches. The Urlinie completes: G→D→C#→B→A. Registers clearing.
